To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a strategy to optimize the switching behavior of rigid, linear, multiple azobenzenes.

the decoupling of the electronic conjugation of multiple azobenzenes by introducing large dihedaral angles between the azobenzene chromophores leads to efficient separation in the absorption spectra of their switching states and hence to almost quantitative E →Z photoisomerization processes.

we have found a way to optimize the photoswitiching efficiency of rigid multiazobenzenes by introducing large dihederal angles between the azobenzene subunits, thus leading to almost quantitative photoswitching of these systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and characterization of a series of linear multiazobenzenes with the focus on the optimization of the photoswitching properties.
the synthesis of rigid rod-like multiazobenzenes with a high degree of decoupling between the azobenzene subunits.
a fundamental understanding of the photochromism of multiazobenzenes and provides a basis for the construction of molecular machines with high switching efficiency.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
electronic decoupling is an effective way to improve the switching efficiency of multiazobenzenes.

electronic decoupling in multiazobenzenes is a powerful strategy to improve their photoswitching behavior and that it is a necessary prerequisite to construct highly efficient molecular machines based on these photochromic switches.

the introduction of a large dihedral angle in the ortho,ortho-positions of the aryl-aryl linker between the two azo chromophores leads to an electronic decoupling of the two azobenzenes and consequently to a quantitative photoswitching of the two azo units.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

by introducing a large dihedral angle into the para positions of the azobenzene unit, a decoupling of the electronic conjugation occurs, which in turn results in a separation of the absorption maxima of the involved switching species.

we have developed a strategy that allows us to construct linear multiazobenzenes with practically quantitative photoswitchable properties by introducing dihedral angles in the aryl-aryl linkers between the azobenzene subunits.
the introduction of large dihedral angle leads to a decoupled system, in which the individual azobenzenes can operate as independent switches.
The main takeaway from our work is that
electronic decoupling can be a useful tool to enhance the photoswitching properties of linear multiazobenzenes.
the decoupling of electronic conjugation in rigid linear multiazobenzenes is a powerful strategy to optimize the switching properties and thus the photoswitching performance of such compounds.
the decoupling approach is a general strategy to optimize the switching behavior of multichromophoric constructs.
